 IMF launches Ukraine loan review that could unlock $1.67 billion
 FILE PHOTO: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Kristalina Georgieva shake hands at a joint meeting during the 81st United Nations General Assembly, in New York City, US, in this handout picture released September 22, 2026. Ukrainian Presidential Press Service/Handout via REUTERS · Reuters Reuters Mon, November 9, 2026 at 6:27 AM CST 2 min read KYIV, Nov 9 (Reuters) - The International Monetary Fund began a review of Ukraine's lending programme on Monday that could unlock $1.67 billion ‌in fresh financing for Kyiv as it struggles to shore up ‌its war-hit economy and plug a looming funding gap. 
 Cooperation with the IMF, Ukraine's key international ​lender, is critical to ensure funding from other partners and help maintain economic stability as the conflict with Russia grinds on and Kyiv faces a multi-billion financing shortfall for next year. 
 "Discussions will cover macroeconomic and fiscal policies, ‌as well as key structural ⁠reforms," Priscilla Toffano, IMF's resident representative in Ukraine, said in a statement. 
 The review combines the second and third assessments ⁠of Ukraine's four-year IMF programme, potentially clearing the way for the disbursement of about $1.67 billion. 
 Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said the meetings would also cover the budget ​and ​international financial aid for 2027. 
 Ukraine's economy, battered ​by more than four years ‌of war, is now in one of its most challenging periods due to intensified Russian air bombardments on businesses, energy infrastructure and revenue-generating sectors. 
 The economy slipped into contraction this year, with the gross domestic product down by 0.7% year-on-year in the third quarter. The central bank expects GDP to ‌slip by 0.4% in 2026. Inflation is ​on the rise, and expected to reach ​12.5% this year. 
 As exports via ​the Black Sea ports are blocked and main exporting ‌sectors — agribusiness and the steel industry — ​are crippled, the budget ​revenues are also falling below the plan. 
 The country faces a massive funding gap of about $70 billion next year, Ukrainian officials have said. 
 The ​central bank said that ‌the IMF's team and Ukrainian officials would hold meetings in ​Lviv and Warsaw with some experts joining the talks online. 
 (Reporting by ​Olena Harmash, Editing by William Maclean)
